chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man: if I buy food from him or buy goods from him on the condition that there is no deficiency/defect on my part (from him), is this valid? And how is the manner of it valid? He said, 'It is not proper (valid).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods with a condition of no deficiency from the seller?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) addresses the validity of a conditional sale where the buyer purchases goods with the stipulation that the seller bears no liability for defects. The Imam’s ruling that this is 'not proper' (la yanbaghi) highlights the Shia juristic preference for clarity in risk allocation, suggesting that while the transaction may be valid, the specific condition of excluding all deficiency liability is legally or practically unsound. This reflects the broader principle in Shia commercial law that guarantees must be explicit and reasonable to avoid ambiguity (gharar).
